    Evaluate a Pipeline

    evaluate_pipeline.Rd

    Evaluates a normalized pipeline in topological order using preloaded raw inputs and direct R function resolution.

    evaluate_pipeline(
  pipeline,
  inputs,
  outputs = pipeline$outputs %||% NULL,
  transform_env = parent.frame(),
  progress = getOption("tsflow.progress", TRUE),
  error_mode = c("fail", "collect")
)

    Arguments

    pipeline

    A `PipelineSpec` object.

    inputs

    A named list of preloaded raw series values. Raw inputs may be R `ts` or `xts` objects keyed by raw series name.

    outputs

    Optional output names to materialize. When provided, execution is pruned to the upstream subgraph required to compute those outputs.

    transform_env

    Environment used to resolve bare transform names during execution. Namespaced transforms such as `stats::lag` are resolved directly.

    progress

    Whether to show execution progress in interactive sessions. Defaults to `getOption("tsflow.progress", TRUE)`.

    error_mode

    Execution failure mode. `"fail"` stops on the first node error. `"collect"` continues evaluating unaffected nodes, records node-level failures, and skips downstream nodes whose dependencies failed.

    Value

    A `PipelineResult` object containing the DAG plan, all computed values, the materialized outputs, and optional error metadata.

    Details

    Transform names may be authored either as explicit namespaced references such as `stats::lag` or as bare names resolved from `transform_env`. The recommended authored form is `pkg::fn`.

    `transform_env` may also define optional evaluation hooks for advanced runtimes. If a function named `tsflow_evaluate_binary_op(op, left, right)` is present, tsflow uses it to evaluate DAG binary operations instead of the default arithmetic dispatch. If a function named `tsflow_postprocess_value(result, context)` is present, tsflow calls it on transform results after the underlying transform function returns. When these hooks are absent, default evaluation behavior is unchanged.

    In interactive sessions, `evaluate_pipeline()` uses `progressr` automatically when it is installed. Existing user-configured `progressr` handlers are respected; if none are configured, tsflow installs a default handler for the current call.
